summary: Every course must be letter graded when the instructor offers a letter grade. The audit checks 40 units of math and science (the calculus, math sequence, EE math and probability courses, physics, and a science elective), a Technology in Society course, 8 units of Engineering Fundamentals with CS 106B, 18 units of EE core, and 31 units across the required course, a design or capstone course and electives, for 100 units in all; a course counts toward one requirement only, except that the WIM course is also your design course. Courses from the School of Engineering's approved science, TiS and fundamentals lists, the 2.0 GPA, the program sheet due the quarter before you graduate, and EE 191W for WIM are checked by hand. Honors adds 10 letter-graded units of EE 191 or 191W at B+ or better, a 3.5 GPA in EE courses, and the thesis and presentation.

OCwKdfpn.why: "Minimum 40 units Math and Science combined, plus three units of TIS, for a total of 43 units." The 43-unit floor sat on the whole School Requirements block, where Engineering Fundamentals units also counted toward it; it is now 40 units over Mathematics and Science, with TiS its own course. Mathematics Sequence: "CME 100 and CME 102 can be substituted for MATH 51 and MATH 53. MATH 52 can be substituted for MATH 51.", so two courses, not one. Science: "3 courses, minimum 12 units", one of them the Science Elective, so Physics is two courses; the Bulletin lists them in the pairs PHYSICS 41 or 61 with EE 65 or PHYSICS 71. The Science Elective is on the School of Engineering's approved list, which is not in the Bulletin text. With the page's course links filled in: "[CME 100] is same as [ENGR 154]. [CME 102] is same as [ENGR 155A]." and "Students may use [CS 109] in place of [EE 178]."
